name: Darwin Initiative Extra

funder.name: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra)

summary: UK government grants of £1 million to £5 million for projects that scale up proven biodiversity and poverty-reduction work from earlier Biodiversity Challenge Funds projects, over two to five years.

geography.label: Darwin Initiative Round 32 eligible countries (within listed biodiversity hotspots)

reporting: Annual and half-year progress reports, reviewed each year, against the project's objectives (outputs, ethics, environmental impact), plus a final report at the end of the award.

eligibility.rule: Works in an eligible biodiversity hotspot or marine/freshwater environment
Promotes economic development and welfare of eligible countries as a primary objective
Follows a clear scaling pathway based on good evidence from previous BCF projects
Is led by or partners with a local or national organisation
Is not a foreign government or agency, except a qualifying university
Is not a Russian organisation involved in the grant
Requests no more than 25% of average annual turnover or income over 3 years

documents: Theory of Change on the provided template, one side of A4 in PDF

status.quote: Applications to Round 32 of Darwin Initiative Extra are now closed.

opens.quote: The latest application round opened on Friday 22nd May 2026.

administered_by.quote: NIRAS Darwin Initiative Administrator; first point of contact for projects and applicants.

geography.quote: In Round 32, parts of 36 countries are eligible.

access.quote: All applications should be submitted via the Flexi-Grant application portal.

window.quote: Applications to Darwin Initiative Extra are a two-stage process, with an interview for shortlisted candidates.

amount.quote: Darwin Initiative Extra will provide grants between £1 million and £5 million, for projects that are on a clear scaling pathway

reporting.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year.

effort.quote: Stage 2 - by invite only - deadline Monday 2nd November 2026.
Shortlisted applicants will be invited to provide clarifications from late December 2026 to 23:59 GMT Monday 11th January 2027.
Shortlisted applicants will be invited to interview (virtual) expected to be between Thursday 14th and Tuesday 19th January 2027.

eligibility.quote: Projects must work within both an eligible country and an eligible hotspot (or marine/freshwater environment).
projects must promote the economic development and welfare of eligible countries (see Annex A) as a primary objective.
for projects that are on a clear scaling pathway: building on good evidence from previous Biodiversity Challenge Funds projects demonstrating the potential to scale further by completion
All projects are required to be led by or partner with local/national organisations of the country/ies in which it is based
Foreign governments and their agencies cannot be Lead Organisations, except for universities that receive government funding
Russian organisations are ineligible to be a Lead Organisation or Partner or involved in any way with any Biodiversity Challenge Fund grant.
The maximum annual value of funds requested should not exceed 25% of the Lead Organisation's average annual turnover/income for the previous 3 years.

after_award.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year.
All projects are required to submit a Final Report at the end of the award.

documents.quote: Theory of Change Required, on template provided
